correctness.rationale: Under iid Bernoulli initial spins and zero-temperature voter rates, coalescing walk duality yields \(G_\ell(0)=(1-m_0^2)\mathbb E[H_A(T_\ell)]\). Finite-mean Pareto renewal gives the exact piecewise H_A. Solving the symmetric rate-two relative-walk hitting-time Laplace equation and substituting \(s=2(\cosh\theta-1)\) produces the exact Mellin beta integral, finite for \(\ell>p\). A Poisson jump bound controls the cutoff correction, and the gamma-ratio limit yields the stated exponent and amplitude. For positive T, the finite-temperature Glauber pair closure plus a \(q^\ell\) harmonic comparison bounds the spatial remainder and isolates common-age variance. Standalone Bessel-density quadratures corroborated 12 parameter cases without being used to infer the theorem. Assumptions, integer/continuous domains, rates, and annealed/quenched distinction were checked explicitly.

originality.rationale: The full 2026 source studies global Pareto reset **magnetization** and explicitly names spatial correlations as an extension. The 2020 global reset source uses Poisson intervals and also limits the work to magnetization. The 2022/2023 voter two-point analysis resets sites independently at Poisson times, a different evolution whose correlation hierarchy does not imply our global Pareto result. Nine actual targeted published-index searches over aliases and gamma-ratio/duality/renewal formulations did not expose an equivalent or stronger claim; nearest hits concern qubit Ising correlations or generic age-residual renewal ranges. Classical coalescence, first-hitting-time Laplace transforms and stationary renewal age are acknowledged as tools, not claimed discoveries. An unindexed or implicit general theorem remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: A classical general coalescing-random-walk plus renewal theorem could imply the claim implicitly without naming global Pareto-reset spins; no proof of absolute novelty.
Search coverage does not exclude unpublished, unindexed, or differently parameterized work.
The fixed initial reset configuration introduces quenched correlations not treated by the annealed theorem.

value.rationale: V K–Nagar arXiv:2602.15495v1 explicitly asks for spatial correlations and domain growth under power-law global resetting. The result gives the naturally defined connected two-spin observable at all large integer separations, with a sharp all-Pareto-exponent amplitude and a nontrivial cutoff error bound. It shows a genuine spatial critical distinction: algebraic decay with continuously tunable \(2(\alpha-1)\) at zero temperature, versus exponential decay of the spatial part for any \(T>0\), correctly accounting for age-induced nondecaying covariance. This is not a known-table recomputation or a relabeling of the original magnetization law.
